2026-10-30.meal: Air-fryer breaded fish fillets with mash, peas & sweetcorn
2026-10-30.note: Half-term starts and Mathilda's had the nursery Halloween party today after gymnastics (9:30am) and swimming (1:30pm) — keeping tea quick, familiar and not too rich.

ingredients: 4 servings mash (fresh potatoes, or microwave pouches for speed)
Butter & milk, for the mash (if making fresh)
steps: Air fry the fish fillets at 190°C for 12-14 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and piping hot.
If making fresh mash, boil chunked potatoes for 15 minutes, drain, then mash with butter and a splash of milk.
Cook the peas and sweetcorn in a pan of boiling water for 4-5 minutes, or microwave.
Drain and serve everything together.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: cut her fillet into pieces and check it's not too hot. Microwave mash pouches work well after a party-food day when there's less time to cook.

2026-10-31.note: This week's one meat night. Hockey open session 9:15-10:15am, then the away match at Sheffield (12-1pm) — a long round trip, plus trick-or-treating this evening. Slow cooker on by 9am so tea's ready whenever we're back.

ingredients: 1 tbsp cornflour, mixed with a splash of water
Crusty bread or mash, to serve
steps: Put the onion, carrots, celery and leeks into the slow cooker.
Add the chicken thighs on top, then the tomatoes, stock, tomato purée and thyme. Season.
Cover and cook on low for 6-7 hours (or high for 3-4) until the chicken is tender and falling apart.
About 20 minutes before serving, stir in the cornflour slurry to thicken, and shred the chicken through the sauce.
Serve with crusty bread or mash.
recipe.tip: On by 9am before hockey and the drive to Sheffield. Mathilda: mash her portion with a fork and check for bones. Freeze any leftovers fully cooled, portioned and labelled for the meal drawer.

2026-11-01.note: Mathilda's Halloween disco 2-3pm at Allegro. Alex away at the Arsenal Ladies match today — keep a labelled portion aside for him to reheat when he's back. A free evening otherwise, so a good day to batch: extra for Tuesday (fridge) and Wednesday (freezer).

ingredients: 18-24 tortillas (enough for tonight, Tuesday and Wednesday)
To serve: salsa, soured cream, lettuce, avocado
steps: Fry the onions and peppers in the oil in your largest pan (or two pans) for 8-10 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the beans, sweetcorn and a splash of water. Take out Mathilda's portion now, keeping it plain.
Split what's left into three roughly equal portions: tonight's, Tuesday's and Wednesday's. Stir the fajita seasoning through tonight's portion and simmer for 5 minutes.
Cool the Tuesday and Wednesday portions within an hour, without adding seasoning to them yet.
Cover and fridge Tuesday's portion. Portion, label and freeze Wednesday's.
Warm tortillas in a dry pan or the microwave. Fill with tonight's filling, cheese and toppings, fold and serve.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep hers mild with no seasoning. Move Wednesday's portion from the freezer to the fridge on Monday night to defrost. Keep a labelled portion of tonight's filling in the fridge for Alex to reheat when he's home from the match.

2026-11-02.note: Free evening, nothing on for tea tonight — a new one to try.

ingredients: 4 salmon fillets, skinned and cut into chunks
Small handful fresh parsley or dill, chopped (optional)
steps: Cook the pasta according to the pack instructions. Save a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
While the pasta cooks, soften the leek in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the salmon chunks and cook gently for 4-5 minutes, turning carefully, until just cooked through.
Stir in the peas and crème fraîche and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Take out Mathilda's portion now, keeping it plain.
Toss the pasta through the rest with the lemon zest and herbs, loosening with a splash of the pasta water. Season and serve.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: flake her salmon finely and check carefully for bones. Keep her portion plain without the lemon zest.

2026-11-03.note: Hull hockey training 6-7pm (Hymers College) plus travel — tea ready for whoever's not driving, kept warm for the rest.

ingredients: Sunday's fridge portion of fajita filling
To serve: salsa, soured cream, lettuce
steps: Tip the filling into a pan with a splash of water.
Heat gently, stirring, until bubbling and piping hot all the way through (about 8 minutes). Or microwave in a covered bowl for 4-5 minutes, stirring halfway.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or the microwave.
Fill with the filling, cheese and toppings, fold and serve.
recipe.tip: Only reheat it once, and check it's piping hot all the way through. Anyone back late from hockey can have theirs microwaved separately.

2026-11-04.note: Hockey Academy Night 6:15-7:45pm (The Lindum) — reheat gets tea done fast either side of the run. Filling was moved to the fridge on Monday night to defrost.

ingredients: Sunday's frozen (now defrosted) portion of fajita filling
To serve: salsa, soured cream, lettuce
steps: Tip the filling into a pan with a splash of water.
Heat gently, stirring, until bubbling and piping hot all the way through (about 10 minutes, a little longer than a fridge portion). Or microwave in a covered bowl for 5-6 minutes, stirring halfway.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or the microwave.
Fill with the filling, cheese and toppings, fold and serve.
recipe.tip: Only reheat it once, and check it's piping hot all the way through, especially since this portion was frozen. Anyone back late from the run can have theirs microwaved separately.

2026-11-05.meal: Mediterranean baked cod with cherry tomatoes, olives & couscous
2026-11-05.note: Free evening, nothing on for tea tonight — a new one to try.

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Put the cod in an ovenproof dish and scatter the cherry tomatoes, garlic and oregano around it. Drizzle with the oil.
Bake for 15-18 minutes, until the fish flakes easily and the tomatoes have softened.
Stir the olives through the tomatoes for the last 5 minutes, for the grown-ups only.
Put the couscous in a bowl, cover with the hot stock, cover with a plate and leave for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Serve the fish and tomatoes over the couscous with a squeeze of lemon.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: leave the olives out of her portion and check carefully for bones.
